knowledge_points.description: Learning from training samples that each carry a label, mapping inputs to outputs.
learning_objectives: State that supervised learning requires labeled training samples.
Recognize classification and regression as supervised tasks.
common_misconceptions: Believing supervised learning can work without any labeled data.
mastery_criteria: Can identify whether a task is supervised given the training data description.

knowledge_points.description: Learning from training samples without labels, discovering internal structure.
learning_objectives: State that unsupervised learning uses unlabeled samples.
Recognize clustering as an unsupervised task.
mastery_criteria: Can identify whether a task is unsupervised given the training data description.

knowledge_points.description: k-nearest neighbors defers explicit modeling; it votes or averages over neighbors at prediction time.
learning_objectives: Explain why kNN is a lazy learner.
Describe the vote/average prediction rule.
common_misconceptions: Believing kNN builds an explicit model during training.
mastery_criteria: Can explain kNN's lazy prediction mechanism.

knowledge_points.description: Choosing k trades off model complexity: small k overfits, large k (up to N) oversimplifies.
learning_objectives: Explain how k affects overfitting and generalization.
common_misconceptions: Believing a smaller k yields a simpler model.
mastery_criteria: Can state the effect of too-small or too-large k.

knowledge_points.description: Minkowski distance measures sample closeness; p=2 is Euclidean, p=1 is Manhattan.
learning_objectives: Compute Euclidean and Manhattan distances between points.
common_misconceptions: Confusing Euclidean distance with Manhattan distance.
mastery_criteria: Can compute Minkowski distances for given points.

knowledge_points.description: Fits a single-feature linear model f(x)=wx+b by minimizing mean squared error (least squares).
learning_objectives: State that least squares minimizes mean squared error.
Compute the closed-form intercept b = y_mean - w*x_mean.
common_misconceptions: Confusing least squares with minimizing absolute error.
mastery_criteria: Can solve a univariate regression from the closed form.

knowledge_points.description: Fits f(x)=w^T x + b over multiple features; the matrix closed form is (X^T X)^-1 X^T Y.
learning_objectives: Express multivariate regression in matrix form.
common_misconceptions: Believing X^T X is always invertible.
mastery_criteria: Can write the multivariate least-squares matrix solution.

knowledge_points.description: Constrains parameter magnitude to improve generalization; Ridge uses L2, LASSO uses L1.
learning_objectives: Distinguish Ridge (L2) from LASSO (L1) regularization.
common_misconceptions: Believing regularization is unrelated to overfitting.
mastery_criteria: Can identify Ridge vs LASSO by their norm penalty.

knowledge_points.description: Minimizes empirical risk plus a parameter-norm penalty, balancing fit and complexity.
learning_objectives: State the SRM objective as L(w,b) + lambda*||w||_p.
common_misconceptions: Confusing structural risk with empirical risk alone.
mastery_criteria: Can write the SRM objective and name its two parts.

knowledge_points.description: Generalizes linear models via a link function; logistic regression is its binary classification case.
learning_objectives: Relate logistic regression to the generalized linear model.
common_misconceptions: Believing logistic regression is ordinary linear regression.
mastery_criteria: Can explain why logistic regression is a classification GLM.

knowledge_points.description: Maps a real value to (0,1), serving as the differentiable surrogate for the unit-step.
learning_objectives: State the sigmoid output range (0,1).
common_misconceptions: Believing sigmoid output can be any real number.
mastery_criteria: Can identify the sigmoid function and its output range.

knowledge_points.description: Estimates logistic regression parameters by maximizing likelihood, equivalent to minimizing cross-entropy.
learning_objectives: State that MLE minimizes cross-entropy loss for logistic regression.
common_misconceptions: Believing MLE is unrelated to cross-entropy.
mastery_criteria: Can write the cross-entropy loss from the likelihood.

knowledge_points.description: Iteratively updates parameters along the negative gradient; the learning rate controls step size.
learning_objectives: State the gradient descent update rule w = w - eta*grad.
common_misconceptions: Believing the learning rate can be arbitrarily large.
mastery_criteria: Can explain the learning-rate role in gradient descent.

knowledge_points.description: Clustering quality has no absolute standard; seek high intra-cluster and low inter-cluster similarity.
learning_objectives: State the intra/inter-cluster similarity principle.
common_misconceptions: Believing clustering quality has one absolute metric.
mastery_criteria: Can judge clustering quality by intra/inter similarity.

knowledge_points.description: Represents each cluster by its sample mean, iterating center selection, assignment, and update.
learning_objectives: Recount the four K-Means steps in order.
common_misconceptions: Believing K-Means can auto-determine the cluster count.
mastery_criteria: Can describe K-Means steps in the correct order.

knowledge_points.description: K-Means needs a preset k, is initialization-sensitive, costly to iterate, and assumes equal feature importance.
learning_objectives: List K-Means limitations.
common_misconceptions: Believing K-Means finds the optimal k automatically.

knowledge_points.description: Clustering discovers data structure standalone or precedes classification; e.g., text clustering and color compression.
learning_objectives: Give examples of clustering applications.
common_misconceptions: Believing clustering is only useful as an end in itself.
mastery_criteria: Can name clustering applications such as text clustering.
